A 🧵 on the most popular advice in product

"We need to focus"
"Focus, focus, focus"
"We need to prioritize"

I hear these things daily in teams everywhere.

But I've come to realize something. Instead of focusing on WHAT to focus on, focus on focusing. Let me explain.

(1/9)

We’ve probably all witnessed the following cycle:

“we need to focus” → lots of effort to prioritize and focus → a great start → things slip → back to the old way (perhaps with a slight makeover).

We see this in ourselves AND in our organizations.

(2/9)

How do you break the cycle?

First, we need to accept that our concerted efforts to prioritize and focus are not enough. We can’t simply will and plan ourselves into focusing. In fact, the premature convergence that comes with these plans is often their undoing.

(3/9)

We work so hard to clarify what we will focus on, that we end up with weaker ideas, and rapid pivots once we figure that out. We quickly lose focus.

Instead, we need to develop a HABIT OF FOCUS. What does that look like?

(4/9)

➡️ Saying “not now” all the time (not just at the start of the year or the quarter).

➡️ Aggressive time blocking.

➡️ Planning at the last responsible moment. No earlier.

and...

(5/9)

➡️ Getting the right people in the same room. Work as a team.

➡️ Aggressively lowering work in progress, even if it means more “slack time”

➡️ Less multitasking.

and...

(6/9)

➡️ Working to *really* clarify our drivers and constraints.

➡️ More starting together. Avoid the temptation to do unfocused work in order to keep other teams "focused".

➡️ Making it safe to “stop the line” when focus is waning.

and...

(7/9)

➡️ Time to do unfocused work and rest your head/brain.

➡️ Know the difference between "efficiency" and "focus". Focus often looks inefficient. Trying to fill every day may feel efficient, but you'll lack focus.

(8/9)

So instead of trying to focus on WHAT to focus on, focus on focusing.

Developing focusing habits, and the rest will fall into place. It is those habits that bring us down, not our heroic efforts to decide on what to focus on.

(9/9)
